title: Actor movement and stop/VM control analysis
scope: Focused static semantic analysis with fresh complete native ASM and pseudocode; current implementation exposes only four one-time Sora movement values.

claims.Finding: Initializes the movement block pointed to by RCX: relative+0 walk2, +4 run8, +8 fallback jump160, +12 angular value, +16 fall cap loaded from parameter table+20, +20 zero. The fall cap is data-driven.
claims.Limitations: The parameter initializer is not a safe general reset: it also resets unrelated movement fields.

claims.Finding: Actor construction calls40A440 at Actor+296 while resetting movement, physics, script and stop-control state.
claims.Limitations: Large constructor has many resource requirements; the trainer only edits four proven fields on an existing actor.

claims.Finding: Normal input chooses Actor+296 below analog magnitude0.8 and Actor+300 at/above0.8, storing the selected speed in Actor+28. Special Action IDs2/24/53 and Action flag8 use other paths; flag8 uses Actor+316.
claims.Limitations: These are normal movement parameters, not universal speed multipliers for every Action.

claims.Finding: Two-instruction base-player input wrapper moves actor RDX to RCX and tail-jumps3A8FA0.
claims.Limitations: Current Sora uses its own equivalent wrapper404FB0.

claims.Finding: Sora input wrapper moves RDX to RCX and tail-jumps the shared3A8FA0 movement-input consumer.
claims.Limitations: Static descriptor750300/vtable5CBA28 slot296 identity is pinned by the trainer; no callback is patched.

claims.Finding: An alternate input helper reads the same walk/run fields and threshold0.8 before updating Actor+28.
claims.Limitations: Its complete call-site reachability was not established; primary Sora proof uses404FB0.

claims.Finding: Movement helper uses selected input magnitude Actor+28 and input vector+16, blends against existing velocity+32, and returns the movement vector.
claims.Limitations: Native float argument registers and scaling make the historical decompiler prototype unreliable; the trainer does not call this function.

claims.Finding: Sora constructor calls base-player initialization with the requested form argument and then installs the same descriptor750300 independently of form.
claims.Limitations: Resource-specific Actions may still override movement. Support is restricted to established Sora forms0..6, not special characters/forms.

claims.Finding: VM adapter decodes an object handle then its actor, returns an encoded pointer to Actor+296, exposing the movement parameter block to scripts.
claims.Limitations: This proves script access can overwrite one-time values; no claim that static direct-writer enumeration covers all generic VM memory stores.

claims.Finding: Reads Actor+304 as fallback jump height and defaults output motionID3. When eligible and positive High Jump level exists, it uses the growth-table height and motion201.
claims.Limitations: Changing base height does not override an enabled High Jump growth level.

claims.Finding: Returns the same fallback or growth-table jump height without the output motion ID.
claims.Limitations: This is a selector, not a writable single resolved-height field.

claims.Finding: Copies movement input to a vector and fills its vertical component from3B59B0; optional flag sets Actor flags288 bit0x10000.
claims.Limitations: This is one jump preparation path and does not prove every jump Action consumes the base parameter.

claims.Finding: Prepares a normal jump using resolved height/motion, calls the native vector jump initializer and selects motion, then sets Actor state fields280/284.
claims.Limitations: Trainer changes the parameter for subsequent consumers; it does not force this Action or restart a jump.

claims.Finding: ABI RCX=Actor and XMM1=height. Configures jump elapsed/peak/base/delta fields240..252; positive height becomes negative vertical delta and duration derives from sqrt(2*height/g).
claims.Limitations: Calling this alone would bypass Action transitions. No engine call is exposed.

claims.Finding: Jump motion computes eased ascent or quadratic descent with constant0.40816328, then caps vertical displacement with timeStep*Actor+312.
claims.Limitations: The cap is not a gravity multiplier. Historical prototype does not represent float register ABI accurately.

claims.Finding: Full ASM establishes output in RDX, Actor in R8 and timestep XMM3; elapsed time advances, vertical result is min(targetY-currentY, timestep*Actor+312), and downward-state flag is updated.
claims.Limitations: Positive downward speed is native coordinate behavior. Special motion flags bypass vertical movement.

claims.Finding: Computes the corresponding vertical displacement from existing elapsed/peak values and caps it with timestep*Actor+312.
claims.Limitations: Does not itself advance elapsed time; trainer does not call it.

claims.Finding: Air-action update applies per-frame0.40816328 acceleration, caps vertical velocity by Actor+312, then scales output displacement by timestep.
claims.Limitations: Additional action parameters affect horizontal/upward behavior. No universal adjustable gravity global is demonstrated.

claims.Finding: ABI RCX=Actor, EDX=stopID, XMM2=duration; if Actor+2488 bit4 is clear, forwards to stop-control block Actor+1612.
claims.Limitations: Not implemented: table and four-slot capacity validation are necessary before a native call.

claims.Finding: VM bank6/index6 adapter decodes actor and forwards integer stop ID plus float duration to3B6730 in the actual native registers.
claims.Limitations: VM metadata arg_count3 and ASM distinguish the float third argument omitted in older pseudocode.

claims.Finding: Searches four stop slots for a matching ID or empty slot, writes ID/duration, then ORs flags from3EED10 for every active slot.
claims.Limitations: With four different occupied IDs the selected slot pointer can remain null. Missing table rows are also dereferenced; unchecked use is unsafe.

claims.Finding: Ticks positive stop timers using global tick factor717480, clears expired IDs and recomputes the aggregate stop mask.
claims.Limitations: Nonpositive timers are not automatically expired; a persistent actor-freeze feature would require ownership and removal policy.

claims.Finding: Clears matching stop IDs among four slots and recomputes aggregate flags for remaining IDs.
claims.Limitations: Removing an ID also owned by a game script would affect its stop; no override API is currently exposed.

claims.Finding: Looks up stop metadata in a loaded sorted four-byte row table at2AE59D8, with row count from header+4.
claims.Limitations: The concrete stop-ID-to-mask contents were not loaded or proven in this round.

claims.Finding: Actor stop predicate combines stop-control maskbit1, category/global conditions, Actor flags288 bit0x400 and another global state.
claims.Limitations: Actor flags288 bit0x400 is also used by visibility paths; it is not a clean AI-only pause bit.

claims.Finding: Main Actor update calls descriptor pre-update+8 before stop-timer/predicate checks. A stopped actor skips central motion/controller/physics updates but retains maintenance and render-list handling.
claims.Limitations: Because pre-update still runs, the mechanism is not established as complete AI/BDX suspension.

claims.Finding: Traverses live actors and applies a supplied stop ID with duration0 only to actor categorybit0x10.
claims.Limitations: This is a native enemy-category stop path; record table contents and ownership are still needed for a trainer feature.

claims.Finding: Traverses actors and removes a supplied stop ID from each actor's stop-control block.
claims.Limitations: Global removal could undo script-owned state; it is documented rather than exposed.

claims.Finding: Script-context gate checks its+300 bit1 and current motion/reaction predicates on the decoded actor.
claims.Limitations: Not identified as an independent AI pause setter; changing it would need additional state-machine proof.

note_on_coverage: 31 complete exports support a focused set of29 claims. Export completeness is not complete semantics; two incidental wrapper bodies are not promoted to new findings.

feature_contract.name: Maximum falling speed
feature_contract.native_initializer: loaded parameter table2AE5760+20; editor preset20 is not a measured native default

pointer_chain: QWORD[base+2A105D0] currentActor; QWORD[Actor+1472] STATUS; packed32[STATUS+616] back to Actor. Packed32[Actor+0] must decode base+750300 and its vtable must be base+5CBA28; input slot+296 must be base+404FB0.
gates: Fresh bridge host/game thread; stable playable field; current actor/list membership; allocated aligned80x632 STATUS pool slot and valid free list; status owner and living HP; charID1; exact Sora descriptor; motion owner backlink; no attachment/deleting/disabled/event/Drive-transition state; readable scene heap; Actor form0..6 matches active form byte. Paused field readouts are allowed, writes are not.
write_contract: Exactly one float32 field is written once after validation; no native function invocation, inline patch, observer hook, retained actor pointer, save write or ability edit.
ownership_restore: There is no held effect or restore lease. Scripts and newly constructed actors may replace the values. Disconnect does not undo completed writes. Profiles apply the four numeric values once when the user explicitly applies them and the current scene gates pass; nothing automatically reapplies after actor/form/scene changes.
policy: Input ranges are conservative trainer limits, not measured engine maxima. Finite current native values outside edit ranges can still be observed.

tests.previous_executed_result: 914 checks, zero failures, /W4 no warnings; no rerun during concurrent Root pipeline.
tests.coverage: All seven Sora forms x four fields x endpoint/fraction cases; whole-Actor byte preservation, finite input bounds, status/list/scene/thread/host/form/ownership gates, real read-only memory and exact capability mask.

limitations: No live movement test was performed.
Growth abilities and special Actions can bypass the base speed/height fields.
Gravity remains a repeated Action constant; a generic low-gravity trainer control is not established.
Per-actor stop/AI work remains research-only because slot capacity, loaded stop masks and ownership need more proof.
The frame/thread model assumes the original engine's update-thread ownership. Arbitrary third-party concurrent writes are not supported.
